description: Running log of the reasoning behind non-obvious dependency/config decisions made while executing bitcore-migration-plan.md. Each entry is one commit and ties it to the plan phase/task it was made under, so a later reader can see why a change was made, not just what changed. Append new entries as new commits land; do not edit past entries except to fix a factual error.

entries.planSection: Phase 2 -- Cut over installation and lock ownership / Task 2.1 -- Introduce npm workspaces and generate the root lock
entries.summary: Real npm-workspace hoisting is permanent (not a transitional cutover artifact) and makes bitcore-node's pinned @types/sinon ambiently reachable from every sibling workspace. bitcore-wallet-service, bitcore-wallet-client, and bitcore-cli never had a reachable @types/sinon under Lerna's per-package isolation, and their test suites grew real reliance on that: ad hoc mock objects and legacy Sinon API usage (e.g. wrappedMethod) that don't satisfy any real @types/sinon version, whether bitcore-node's outdated 4.3.3 pin or bitcore-cli's own much newer sinon@^21.0.0 (which doesn't ship its own bundled types either). Follow-up to retire this by modernizing each package's test doubles is tracked in .idea/npm-workspaces/follow-up/bitcore-sinon-typing-debt.md.

changes.change: Added a `paths` entry redirecting the `sinon` module specifier to a new local ./types/sinon-shim.d.ts.
changes.reasoning: Restores this package's tests to the untyped `sinon` behavior they were always actually written against (see the new shim file's own reasoning), rather than type-checking against bitcore-node's ambiently-hoisted @types/sinon@4.3.3, which this package's mocks don't satisfy.

changes.change: New file: `declare const sinon: any; export = sinon;`
changes.reasoning: The real `sinon` package this shim's import specifier is redirected away from is unaffected at runtime -- only this package's own TypeScript type-checking of the `sinon` import changes, back to the implicit `any` it always had under Lerna's isolated installs.

changes.change: Added a `paths` entry redirecting the `sinon` module specifier to a new local ./types/sinon-shim.d.ts.
changes.reasoning: Same reasoning as bitcore-wallet-service's identical change: restores this package's tests to their always-implicit-any `sinon` typing.

changes.change: New file: `declare const sinon: any; export = sinon;`
changes.reasoning: Same shim pattern as bitcore-wallet-service's.

changes.change: Added a `paths` object (this package had none before) with a `sinon` entry redirecting to a new local ./types/sinon-shim.d.ts.
changes.reasoning: Same underlying gap, with an added wrinkle: bitcore-cli's own sinon@^21.0.0 doesn't ship its own bundled TypeScript types, so without this shim it falls back to bitcore-node's ancient @types/sinon@4.3.3 -- a version mismatch far larger than in the other two packages (Sinon 4 vs Sinon 21), rejecting even ordinary usage like `sinon.stub(API.prototype, 'constructor')`.

changes.change: New file: `declare const sinon: any; export = sinon;`
changes.reasoning: Same shim pattern as the other two packages'.

entries.planSection: Phase 2 -- Cut over installation and lock ownership / Task 2.1 -- Introduce npm workspaces and generate the root lock
entries.summary: Real npm-workspace hoisting (proven for the first time against this repo's actual dependency graph, not a synthetic fixture -- see artifacts/workspaces/task2.1/evidence.md) exposed three packages that had always implicitly relied on @types/* resolution Lerna's per-package-isolated installs happened to provide for them, or that hoisting now routes to the wrong sibling's pinned version. Fixed each by declaring the package's own correct devDependency instead of continuing to depend on which sibling wins the hoist.

changes.change: Added devDependency @types/secp256k1@^4.0.7.
changes.reasoning: bitcore-node's src/utils/auth.ts calls secp256k1.ecdsaVerify(...), a real API on its installed secp256k1@4.0.3, but the package never declared its own @types/secp256k1. Under Lerna's isolated installs this was implicit `any` (tsconfig.json sets noImplicitAny: false) and the gap was invisible. Under real hoisting it instead inherits bitcore-client's exact @types/secp256k1@3.5.0 pin, which lacks ecdsaSign/ecdsaVerify -- a real tsc failure. ^4.0.7 matches bitcore-wallet-service's already-established fix for the identical gap (see below) and the installed secp256k1@4.0.3 runtime version.

changes.change: Added @types/express@^4.17.21, @types/request-promise-native@^1.0.15, and @types/secp256k1@^4.0.7. Re-pinned @types/node from "^22.10.10" to exact "22.19.15" and @types/request from "^2.48.1" to exact "2.48.13".
changes.reasoning: Two different problems, both only visible under real hoisting. (1) Missing declarations: this package directly uses express, request-promise-native, and (transitively, via its own blockchainexplorers/v8.ts) secp256k1, but only ever declared @types/request for the group -- the other three were always implicit `any` under Lerna. Real hoisting makes some sibling's own pin ambiently reachable instead (bitcore-node's @types/express@4.17.21, bitcore-client's @types/request-promise-native, bitcore-client's older @types/secp256k1@3.5.0), which happened to work for @types/express but not for the other two, so all three are now declared directly. (2) Version reversion: @types/node and @types/request both used caret ranges here, and under Lerna's isolated installs each resolved independently to the newest matching patch at lock-generation time (22.19.15 and 2.48.13, confirmed from this package's pre-migration package-lock.json, git history). Under real hoisting, two *other* packages (bitcore-client, bitcore-node) each pin an older *exact* version of the same two libraries, and npm's single shared hoisted copy ends up being one of those older exact pins instead of the newest range match -- and both older versions have a real typing difference this package's code hits (a header-value indexing difference in @types/node@22.13.1 vs 22.19.15; a `Cannot use namespace as a type` regression specific to @types/request@2.48.1 vs 2.48.13). Re-pinning this package's own exact versions forces npm to nest its own correctly-versioned copies rather than sharing whichever sibling's pin wins the hoist.

changes.change: Reverted the @solana/kit devDependency from "2.3.0" back to "2.1.0".
changes.reasoning: crypto-wallet-core has pinned @solana/kit to an exact 2.1.0 since a Dec 2025 commit ('crypto-rpc to use CWC dependencies', Kenny Joseph) specifically so that crypto-rpc would share its exact installed copy rather than get its own: @solana/kit exports a nominally-branded Address type, so two distinct-but-semver-compatible copies of the package are not type-compatible with each other. A same-day-as-this-fix commit ('fix crypto-rpc deps') had added @solana/kit as a new devDependency of crypto-rpc, but at 2.3.0 -- diverging from crypto-wallet-core's pin (the accompanying @solana-program/* versions added in that same commit did correctly match crypto-wallet-core's pins; only @solana/kit itself didn't). Under real hoisting this produced two separate installed copies of @solana/kit (and its nested @solana/addresses), and TypeScript's nominal branding broke crypto-wallet-core's own tsc build across its sol/spl transaction code with a cascade of Address-type-mismatch errors. Reverting to 2.1.0 restores the single shared instance Kenny's commit established; confirmed via the regenerated lock resolving to one root-hoisted @solana/kit@2.1.0 with no nested copies.

entries.planSection: Phase 2 -- Cut over installation and lock ownership / Task 2.1 -- Introduce npm workspaces and generate the root lock
entries.summary: bitcore-wallet-service's route/auth code reads several properties off Express's `Request` object (`copayer`, `session`, `walletId`, `copayerId`, `isSupportStaff`, `redirectedUrl`) that middleware genuinely attaches at runtime, but that Express's own types have no way to know about. Under Lerna's isolated installs this package never had a reachable @types/express (only bitcore-node declares it), so every one of these accesses type-checked as implicit `any` and the gap was invisible. Real hoisting makes bitcore-node's @types/express ambiently reachable here too, so the real Request type applies and every access to an undeclared property becomes a real tsc error.

changes.change: Added a `declare global { namespace Express { interface Request { ... } } }` block declaring the six properties, typed against where each is actually assigned (context.ts, walletdata.ts, authRequest.ts, authTssRequest.ts) -- e.g. `copayer?: Copayer` because `authRequest.ts` assigns the real return value of its own `withSession`/`withSignature` helpers (`Promise<Copayer>`) to `req.copayer`.
changes.reasoning: This is TypeScript declaration merging, not an override: @types/express-serve-static-core itself declares `interface Request {}` inside the exact same `declare global { namespace Express { ... } }` shape, deliberately empty so downstream code can merge more members into it, and its own exported `express.Request` type is literally defined as `interface Request<...> extends http.IncomingMessage, Express.Request` -- i.e. it already extends this same global interface. Adding properties here does not replace or narrow Express's Request type; it adds six more optional properties to the one merged interface that express.Request already extends, which is the standard, Express-documented mechanism for this (the alternative -- casting `req as any` at every one of the ~10 call sites that read these properties -- would be both more code and would suppress real checking of everything else on `req` at each of those sites, not just the added properties). The declaration lives in `declare global`, so it is visible everywhere in this package's own single tsc compilation (which is the only place it needs to be); each package has its own separate tsc invocation under this monorepo's real per-package compile step, so this does not leak into any other workspace's compilation, and the file is under `src/types/` (not the package's public entry point), so nothing external imports it either.

entries.planSection: Phase 2 -- Cut over installation and lock ownership / Task 2.1 -- Introduce npm workspaces and generate the root lock
entries.summary: Each change in this commit fixes a real tsc failure directly reproduced under a real `npm ci` against this repo's actual hoisted install (not a synthetic fixture or a guess) -- confirmed by running the real per-package compile with the change removed and seeing the exact error return. Two categories: modern @types/express is now reachable (and precise) for the first time in bitcore-wallet-service, so req.query/req.headers's real, wider types (string | ParsedQs | array; string | string[]) are checked at real call sites for the first time; and an unrelated transitive @types/superagent (a real dependency of bitcore-tss's @bitgo/sdk-lib-mpc) is now ambiently reachable in bitcore-wallet-client, where two fields' test doubles never implemented the real SuperAgentRequest shape.

changes.change: `static r = superagent;` (inferred type) -> `static r: any = superagent;`
changes.reasoning: Real @types/superagent@4.1.15 (from bitcore-tss's @bitgo/sdk-lib-mpc dependency, not declared by this package or anything it directly depends on) is now ambiently reachable, so this field's type is no longer implicit `any` -- but test code assigns lightweight fakes (e.g. `{ get: _url => ({ set, query, end }) }`) to it that don't implement the real SuperAgentRequest interface (cookies, method, url, abort, and dozens more). Per Task 2.1's principle (fix tests, don't loosen production types, unless the fix is test-code surgery out of this task's scope), this is logged as debt in the sinon-typing-debt follow-up doc rather than fixed by rewriting the mocks now.

changes.change: `static request = superagent;` (inferred type) -> `static request: any = superagent;`
changes.reasoning: Identical to paypro.ts's change above -- same field pattern, same fake-request test doubles, same reachable-but-mismatched @types/superagent.

changes.change: `checkNumberFormat(req.query.numberFormat, res)` -> `checkNumberFormat(req.query.numberFormat as string, res)` at all 5 call sites.
changes.reasoning: `checkNumberFormat` is typed `(numberFormat: string | undefined, res: express.Response) => void`. Modern @types/express types `req.query.x` as `string | ParsedQs | (string | ParsedQs)[]`, which was never checked here before (this package had no reachable @types/express under Lerna). In practice this query parameter is always a plain string or absent (Express's default parser only produces ParsedQs/array shapes for bracket/array query syntax, e.g. `?numberFormat[]=x`, which nothing sends here); the assertion reflects that real-world constraint rather than adding runtime validation for it.

changes.change: `const copayerId = req.headers['x-identity'];` -> `... as string;` at all 7 call sites.
changes.reasoning: @types/node types header values as `string | string[] | undefined` in general (some headers, like set-cookie, really can repeat as an array), now checked here for the first time. In practice a plain custom header like `x-identity` is always folded into a single string by Node's own HTTP parser when a client sends it more than once -- it is not one of the small set of headers Node treats as array-valued -- so this reflects that real constraint.

changes.change: `router.handle(req, res)` -> `(router as any).handle(req, res)`; `Array.isArray(req.query.addresses) ? req.query.addresses : req.query.addresses.split(',')` -> `Array.isArray(req.query.addresses) ? req.query.addresses.map(String) : String(req.query.addresses).split(',')`.
changes.reasoning: `Router.handle` is a real Express method that re-dispatches a request through the same router without an HTTP round-trip; it exists at runtime but Express deliberately does not publish it in its own types, so some cast is required regardless of hoisting -- `any` was chosen since there is no more-precise typed alternative to reach for here (a local type intersection adding just `handle` with a hand-written signature was considered and rejected as not worth its own maintenance burden for one internal-API call). The `.split(',')` fix is unrelated and not an `any`/assertion at all: the prior code left the true (array) branch of the ternary typed as `(string | ParsedQs)[]`, not `string[]`, which is what `opts.addresses` requires; `.map(String)` makes both ternary branches produce real `string[]` values.

changes.change: Four `req.query.x`/`req.query['x']` accesses (`numberFormat` x2, `walletCheck`, `account`) cast `as string` at their real call sites (`checkNumberFormat`, `['1','true'].includes(...)`, `parseInt(...)`).
changes.reasoning: Same category as transactions.ts above -- these are all single, non-repeated query parameters that are always plain strings in practice; the assertions reflect that, not runtime validation for the theoretical array/object case.

entries.planSection: Phase 2 -- Cut over installation and lock ownership / Task 2.1 -- Introduce npm workspaces and generate the root lock
entries.summary: Corrects the direction of an earlier fix in this same task. V8's `request` field was loosened to `any` to unblock compilation (real @types/request-promise-native became reachable and its precise type, `typeof request`, broke test mocks that only implement one method each). Per this project's rule that production types should stay accurate and test doubles should be the ones that adapt, reverted to the precise type and fixed the test mocks instead.

changes.change: `request: any;` / `request?: any;` -> `request: typeof request;` / `request?: typeof request;`.
changes.reasoning: This is the exact fix the compiler itself suggested ("Did you mean 'typeof request'?") when the original code (`request: request;` -- a value used directly as a type, invalid TypeScript, silently accepted only because the whole module was implicit `any` before hoisting) first failed. No test files were ever deleted or had content removed to get here; the earlier `any` was reverted and this precise type substituted instead.

changes.change: Added `import * as request from 'request-promise-native';` (the identical import style v8.ts itself uses -- see below for why that specific style matters) and appended `as unknown as typeof request` to each of the 7 `const fakeRequest = { get: sinon.stub()... }` declarations.
changes.reasoning: Each `fakeRequest` is a deliberate minimal test double (only the one method that specific test actually exercises), not a real request-promise-native client, so it cannot structurally satisfy the real `RequestAPI` interface (dozens of methods: post, put, del, defaults, debug, ...) on its own -- `as unknown as X` is the standard, narrowly-scoped TypeScript idiom for asserting a deliberate partial substitute at its one injection point, as opposed to loosening the production field everything else depends on. One real pitfall hit and resolved here: the test's first attempt imported request-promise-native as a default import (`import type request from 'request-promise-native'`), which under this tsconfig's `esModuleInterop` resolves to a *different* type shape than v8.ts's own `import * as request from 'request-promise-native'` (namespace import) -- confirmed empirically by the resulting tsc error demanding an unrelated `default`-wrapped shape. Matching v8.ts's exact import style makes `typeof request` refer to the identical type in both files, which is what actually made the cast succeed.

entries.planSection: Phase 2 -- Cut over installation and lock ownership / Task 2.2 -- Verify cold installation, native modules, and CLI linking
entries.summary: A real cold-install run on the pinned Node 22 Linux environment (node:22.16.0-bookworm, the exact image family this project uses for CI/production, run in a real Docker container -- not reasoned about) hung indefinitely on test/workspaces/compile.test.cjs's signal-handling tests, previously verified only on macOS. Root-caused with a minimal, direct `sh -c` reproduction (recorded in artifacts/workspaces/task2.2/evidence.md) rather than guessed: npm always runs a package's own script through `/bin/sh -c '<script>'`, and this project's two supported platforms' default `/bin/sh` disagree about what that produces. macOS's `/bin/sh` execve-replaces itself for a simple trailing command like `node compile.js`, leaving no distinct shell process in the tree. Debian/Ubuntu's `/bin/sh` (dash -- the base of every `node:*-bookworm` image this project uses) forks a real, separate child instead, and dash does not relay a signal it receives on to that child; it just dies immediately, permanently orphaning the still-running compile step and hanging anything waiting on it. This is a genuine, permanent platform fact about dash's own signal handling, not a transient sandbox limitation -- it would reproduce identically on real Linux CI/developer machines.

changes.change: runWorkspaceCompile now walks npm's real OS descendants (via `pgrep -P`) and signals only the leaf processes directly, in addition to signaling npm itself as before; it then waits for those leaves' real exit (polling, since there is no `exit` event for a process this runner did not spawn directly) before resolving.
changes.reasoning: Signaling only npm was already proven insufficient (the Linux hang above); the first fix attempted instead broadcast the signal to npm's whole process group (`detached: true` + negative-pid kill), which reaches every descendant including intermediate shells, but that reintroduces a different problem: dash, when signaled directly, dies immediately without observing its own child's real exit, which made npm's own reported exit -- and this runner's resolution of the whole compile step -- happen before the real leaf script had actually finished, undoing this same function's pre-existing, deliberately-tested guarantee (see the runWorkspaceCompile doc comment, unchanged) that an interrupted runner never reports done before the child has actually terminated. The final design signals only leaves (skipping every intermediate shell, so each one still exits normally once its own child does, keeping npm's own relay-and-wait behavior intact wherever it already works) and separately awaits those leaves' own real termination (since on the platforms where an intermediate shell exists, npm's own `exit` event no longer reflects them). Verified stable across 3 consecutive full orchestration-suite runs (92/92) on both a real `node:22.16.0-bookworm` container and macOS.

changes.change: The one assertion checking npm's own reported exit code for an interrupted child (`result.code === 0`) now accepts either that or `(code === null && signal === 'SIGTERM')`.
changes.reasoning: What npm itself reports for its own exit is a real, permanent, platform-dependent fact once the leaf is confirmed reached (see summary above): on macOS npm's own child IS the leaf (no intermediate shell survives), so npm reports a clean 0 directly; on Debian/Ubuntu's dash-based `/bin/sh`, npm's own child is a distinct shell that dies from the very signal npm relays to it, before it can observe or reflect the leaf's own graceful exit, so npm instead reports that shell's signal death. Per this project's rule to prefer fixing test code over loosening production types where a real fix requires test-code surgery: this is not production code, and the assertion was checking an implementation detail (which of two legitimate npm-reported shapes occurred) rather than the actual invariant, which the test already separately verifies via the marker file proving the real leaf received and handled the signal -- that assertion is unchanged.

entries.planSection: Phase 3 -- Preserve developer commands and CI / Task 3.1 -- Replace root and legacy command routing
entries.summary: Before changing anything, compared the real root package.json against this task's own acceptance list and found the 17 test:<directory> aliases, node/bws, watch, and build:docker already matched the target design exactly -- introduced by Task 2.1's coordinated manifest/script cutover, not this task. The genuinely remaining work was packages/build, ci.sh's stale example, and two package Makefiles using hardcoded .bin paths; each is a real, independently-verified fix rather than a restatement of already-done work.

changes.change: Replaced the hardcoded, unscoped, caller-cwd-relative compile loop (missing bitcore-logging/CLI/node) with a delegation to `npm --prefix <script-relative-root> run compile`, i.e. the canonical scripts/workspaces/compile.cjs runner, with `set -e`.
changes.reasoning: The old script's `cd $i && npm run compile || (echo ERROR && exit) && cd ..` idiom has a real bug, reproduced standalone with a synthetic 3-module version: `exit` inside the `(... && exit)` subshell only exits that subshell, so the loop actually continues past every module's failure and the whole script always exits 0 -- confirmed by running the equivalent idiom with a deliberately failing first module and observing exit 0 with all three modules 'run'. The new version was verified from three different callers' cwd (a disposable /tmp dir, packages/, and the repo root), each producing an identical full seven-package `[compile] All seven packages compiled successfully, in order.` from the already-proven compile runner.

changes.change: Corrected the --help example from the never-existing `npm run ci:bitcore-node` to the real `npm run test:bitcore-node` alias.
changes.reasoning: Grepped every package.json and the whole tree (excluding node_modules and this plan document) for `ci:bitcore` / `"ci:` and found no script by that name anywhere; it was always a documentation typo, not a removed or renamed script. Documentation-only change to a --help string; bash -n confirmed the file still parses.

changes.change: Removed (git rm).
changes.reasoning: Invoked `./node_modules/.bin/mocha` and istanbul directly; unreferenced by any script, doc, or CI job (grepped .circleci/config.yml and both packages' READMEs for `make`/`Makefile`, no hits); and now unsatisfiable regardless, since Task 1.4 established root as the sole declared owner of mocha/nyc for this package. The package's real `npm test` (nyc mocha, already what root's test:bitcore-wallet-service alias runs) covers the same ground without the stale coverage tool or hardcoded bin path.

changes.change: Removed (git rm).
changes.reasoning: Same disposition as wallet-service's Makefile: unreferenced anywhere, and its `all`/`clean` targets built a browserify bundle (bitcore-wallet-client.js) that nothing in the repository imports or serves (grepped for the filename across the package, no hits) -- a dead artifact of a bundling step this package's real scripts no longer perform.

entries.planSection: Phase 3 -- Preserve developer commands and CI / Task 3.3 -- Update CircleCI installation, caching, and test inventory
entries.summary: Task 2.1's own evidence claimed a root .npmrc (engine-strict=false) was added, but no commit on this branch ever created it (git log --all -- .npmrc shows only a pre-migration, unrelated 'mv .npmrc to bitcore-tss'). This surfaced while designing this task's CI cache key, which needs to checksum an install-affecting .npmrc per the plan's target design item 4 and acceptance-spec Sec3. Added it directly rather than leaving the target-design requirement unmet, since it is a small, additive, zero-behavior-change fix (matches npm's own engine-strict default) with no test surface.

changes.change: New file: engine-strict=false.
changes.reasoning: socks5-client@0.3.6 (used by all three P2P packages) declares engines.node: 0.x, so npm's graph-wide strict engine check would reject the existing dependency graph outright. Real engine compatibility is instead enforced after install by scripts/workspaces/verify.cjs (engines mode), wired into root postinstall, which allows only that one documented exception and fails on every other mismatch. Confirmed the addition changes nothing observable (npm config get engine-strict is false both before and after, since that already matches npm's own default) and reverified check-runtime.cjs/verify.cjs manifests/engines/lock all still pass.

changes.change: Rewrote installation, caching, and test-job inventory: Node/npm pinned to 22.16.0/10.9.2 with npm force-installed explicitly; removed create_concatenated_package_lock and all combined-package-lock.txt references; replaced restored-node_modules caching with npm-download-cache (~/.npm) keyed on OS/arch, the exact Node/npm pair, and package-lock.json/.npmrc checksums; added explicit check-runtime.cjs preflight before npm ci and each job's npm run compile; added verify.cjs manifests/lock/engines/links/artifacts, npm ls, and the orchestration test suite to the build job; removed the disabled build-crypto-rpc job and its now-unused executor; added bitcore-p2p-cash/bitcore-p2p-doge jobs; removed use_python2/pyenv-2.7 setup.
changes.reasoning: Each change maps directly to Task 3.3's Work list. The npm-download-cache redesign follows the plan's explicit instruction ('cache npm's download cache rather than restored installed trees... always run npm ci whether the cache hits or misses'): the old cache restored ~20 explicit per-package node_modules paths behind an already-disabled restore step, which is both redundant (persist_to_workspace already carries the full post-install tree to every test job) and the wrong target once there is one hoisted root install. The Python 2 removal is backed by Task 2.2's real node:22.16.0-bookworm Linux cold-install log (artifacts/workspaces/task2.2/linux-final-full-cold-sequence.log), which shows every native module's node-gyp compile already resolving Python 3.11.2 with zero Python 2 use -- a real measurement of this exact dependency graph on Node 22, not an assumption. build-crypto-rpc was already commented out of the workflow (dead) and only persisted the RPC package directory alone, insufficient once its dependencies live at the workspace root; the plan explicitly prefers removing this disabled path over repairing it, since the common build job already supplies every active test job including crypto-rpc's own. The p2p-cash/p2p-doge additions were verified as an exact 17-entry match against package.json's test:* scripts via a programmatic diff, not eyeballed. Config validity (including the absence of any remaining Lerna/combined-package-lock reference in the fully expanded config) was confirmed with the real circleci CLI (circleci config validate / circleci config process), installed for this task via Homebrew. crypto-rpc's own Docker-based test path is left unvalidated end-to-end, per the plan's own dependency line ('validate Docker test jobs after Phase 4') -- its docker-compose.yml build context is still package-local, which Task 4.2 is scoped to fix.
